topics.title: Risk Assessments
topics.intro: Plain-English UK guidance on writing risk assessments, common mistakes, and ready-to-use templates.

faq.q: Do I legally need a written risk assessment?
faq.a: Often yes in practice — especially if you have employees or higher-risk work. Even when not strictly required, recording your assessment is usually the quickest way to prove you’ve done it properly.

faq.q: How often should I review it?
faq.a: Review when something changes (process, people, equipment, substances, layout) or after an incident/near miss. Otherwise set a sensible review date (e.g., annually).
